chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudaylah from Hammad from Abu Basir said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If you are in a land of fear and you fear a thief or a beast, then pray the obligatory prayer while you are on your mount.'
And from him, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who fears from a beast or a thief, how does he pray? He said: 'He says Takbir and gestures with his head.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform the obligatory prayer when fearing danger from thieves or beasts?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of Salat al-Khawf, emphasizing that when fear of a thief or beast is imminent, the believer may pray while mounted on their animal. The method prescribed—gesturing with the head (i'nam) rather than full bowing (ruku) and prostration (sujud)—reflects the principle of ease (taysir) in worship during genuine danger, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding the flexibility of prayer postures.
